skill.name: markdown-toc
skill.description: Generate and update tables of contents in Markdown files with configurable heading levels, insertion modes, and batch processing options.
skill.summary: Generate Markdown tables of contents with preview, batch processing, and marker-based insertion support.
skill.author: Emasoft

security_audit.summary: All static findings are Markdown code fences or inline code formatting, not executable Ruby or shell backtick usage. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, network access, or secret handling was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: | `--dry-run` | false | Preview TOC without modifying files |
| `--title TEXT` | "Table of Contents" | Custom TOC title |
| `--insert MODE` | auto | Insertion mode: auto, top, marker |
| `--marker TEXT` | `<!-- TOC -->` | Custom marker for marker mode |
1. Replace existing `## Table of Contents` section
2. Insert after first `---` separator (common README pattern)
File may only have H1 headers. Use `--min-level 1`.
Use `--insert marker` with explicit markers for precise control.
Check for duplicate headers (GitHub appends `-1`, `-2`, etc.).

content.value_statement: Large Markdown projects become hard to navigate when headings change. This skill helps generate, preview, and update tables of contents across files.
actual_capabilities: Generate table of contents entries from Markdown headings.
Preview planned table of contents changes with dry run command examples.
Handle multiple files, directories, glob patterns, and recursive processing.
Limit included headings with minimum and maximum heading level options.
Insert or replace tables of contents at the top, automatically, or between markers.
Create GitHub-style anchors for common Markdown heading formats.
limitations: It describes commands for a Python script; this audited package only includes the skill instructions.
Running without dry run can modify Markdown files in place.
Duplicate headings may still need manual link checks after generation.
It skips code blocks, YAML frontmatter, and headings outside configured levels.

use_cases.title: Refresh Project Documentation
use_cases.description: Update README and docs tables of contents after headings change.

use_cases.title: Prepare Open Source Releases
use_cases.description: Preview and standardize navigation links before publishing release notes or guides.

use_cases.title: Organize Large Doc Sets
use_cases.description: Apply consistent table of contents settings across folders and guide collections.

prompt_templates.title: Preview One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check before editing a README.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a table of contents preview for README.md. Use the default heading levels and explain where it will be inserted.

prompt_templates.title: Update Documentation Folder
prompt_templates.scenario: Process several Markdown files with a dry run first.
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview table of contents updates for all Markdown files in docs. Then list the files that would change.

prompt_templates.title: Use Custom Heading Levels
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a deeper table of contents for a long guide.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a table of contents for README.md using headings from level 1 through level 4. Preview the result before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Marker Insertion
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for controlled replacement zones.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update tables of contents between explicit markers across docs. Use recursive processing and show any files without matching markers.

output_examples.input: A README with Installation, Usage, Advanced Usage, and Contributing headings.
output_examples.output: A titled table of contents with nested links that match the heading hierarchy.

output_examples.input: A docs folder containing several Markdown guides.
output_examples.output: A preview showing each processed file, the generated table of contents, and the heading count.

output_examples.input: A guide with explicit table of contents markers.
output_examples.output: The content between the markers is replaced while surrounding text remains unchanged.

best_practices: Run a dry run before applying changes to project documentation.
Use marker mode when each file needs a precise replacement location.
Review generated links when documents contain repeated or unusual headings.
anti_patterns: Do not run recursive updates without checking the preview first.
Do not mix different heading level rules across related documentation without a reason.
Do not rely on automatic placement when a document has a strict template.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps generate and update tables of contents for Markdown files.

faq.question: Can it preview changes before editing files?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented dry run mode shows the planned table of contents without modifying files.

faq.question: Can it process more than one file?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions cover multiple paths, glob patterns, directories, and recursive processing.

faq.question: Can I control which heading levels appear?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents minimum and maximum heading level options.

faq.question: Where can the table of contents be inserted?
faq.answer: It supports automatic placement, top placement, and marker-based replacement.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No external service is described. The documented workflow uses a local Python script.
